licensure.disciplinary_grounds.rationale: These nine buckets cover the clear natural clusters across all states: fraud in obtaining/using credentials, criminal convictions, quality-of-care failures (negligence/incompetence/malpractice), substance and mental/physical impairment, unlicensed practice and aiding, advertising deception, improper financial practices (fee fraud, splitting, overcharging), broad unprofessional/immoral/sexual-misconduct conduct, and the large residual of law/rule/order/reporting violations that don't fit the more specific clusters.

profession_specific.laser_procedures_aut.rationale: The items cluster into specific named procedures (capsulotomy, trabeculoplasty, iridotomy), broad categorical authorizations (therapeutic, refractive, or board-rule-defined), diagnostic-only uses, and non-laser light therapies (IPL/LLLT), which together cover the full distribution without significant overlap.

profession_specific.minor_surgical_proce.rationale: These nine buckets cleanly map to the anatomical and procedural clusters visible in the data: lash removal, corneal debridement/scraping/puncture, lacrimal duct/plug procedures, injections (anesthetics, steroids, botulinum, epinephrine), excision or drainage of chalazia and eyelid lesions, foreign body extraction, structural eyelid repair/laceration closure, non-laser/IPL light therapies, and culture/specimen collection—leaving no meaningful item without a natural home.

profession_specific.controlled_substance.rationale: These buckets capture the dominant patterns: outright Schedule I bans, outright Schedule II bans, the very common hydrocodone carve-out from Schedule II prohibitions, permissive-but-restricted Schedule III–V access, explicit short-supply (72-hour/3-day/5-day) limits, exclusions of non-controlled drug classes (immunosuppressives, antifungals, steroids, etc.), and the handful of items that reference statutory sections or formularies without specifying a schedule.

profession_specific.tiered_license_types.rationale: Optometry tiered licenses cluster around a base credential, then escalate through diagnostic pharmaceutical authority, therapeutic pharmaceutical authority, expanded/advanced therapeutic or procedural authority, glaucoma-specific endorsements, surgical (laser) authority, and a residual tier for faculty/limited or otherwise non-standard credentials.

profession_specific.specialty_certificat.rationale: The items cluster naturally by pharmaceutical route/type (diagnostic topical, therapeutic topical, oral, injectable), specific disease-area certifications (glaucoma), procedural scope expansions (advanced procedures/laser/surgery), immunization authority, and the rare opt-out category of practicing without pharmaceutical agents — covering the full distribution without an unwieldy catch-all.
